exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. Practical Python 3.10-3.14 fluency track; official Python documentation and selected AnyIO/HTTPX docs reviewed 2026-09-19.

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; progressively harder typed code recall provides the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Python Fluency is practical coding retrieval, not beginner trivia or a certification. Questions use progressive recall depth: guided -> recall -> construct -> fluency. Short literals stay on one line where readable, unfamiliar data shapes and intent are explained, and most questions have one meaningful blank.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(coro) creates and manages an event loop for a top-level coroutine and closes it when the coroutine completes.

reveal.text: asyncio.run(coro) creates and manages an event loop for a top-level coroutine and closes it when the coroutine completes.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ common script entry point is asyncio.run(main()).

reveal.text: A common script entry point is asyncio.run(main()).

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________() cannot be called while another asyncio event loop is already running in the same thread.

reveal.text: asyncio.run() cannot be called while another asyncio event loop is already running in the same thread.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(*aws) runs awaitables concurrently and returns successful results in the same order as the supplied awaitables.

reveal.text: asyncio.gather(*aws) runs awaitables concurrently and returns successful results in the same order as the supplied awaitables.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ asyncio.gather(*(fetch_user(i) for i in ids)) is a compact ordered fan-out/fan-in pattern.

reveal.text: await asyncio.gather(*(fetch_user(i) for i in ids)) is a compact ordered fan-out/fan-in pattern.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ is an async context manager for structured concurrency: created tasks are awaited when the context exits and failures are handled as a group.

reveal.text: asyncio.TaskGroup is an async context manager for structured concurrency: created tasks are awaited when the context exits and failures are handled as a group.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg: tg.create_task(work()) keeps related child tasks scoped to the block.

reveal.text: async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg: tg.create_task(work()) keeps related child tasks scoped to the block.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ not swallow CancelledError inside TaskGroup children without a deliberate reason; structured-concurrency machinery relies on cancellation.

reveal.text: Do not swallow CancelledError inside TaskGroup children without a deliberate reason; structured-concurrency machinery relies on cancellation.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ limits how many tasks may enter a protected section concurrently by maintaining an async counter.

reveal.text: asyncio.Semaphore limits how many tasks may enter a protected section concurrently by maintaining an async counter.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ with semaphore: return await fetch(url) is the preferred acquire/release pattern.

reveal.text: async with semaphore: return await fetch(url) is the preferred acquire/release pattern.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ synchronization primitives are for tasks in an event loop; they are not thread-safe synchronization tools.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ coordinates producers and consumers without blocking the event loop; a positive maxsize makes put() wait when the queue is full.

reveal.text: asyncio.Queue coordinates producers and consumers without blocking the event loop; a positive maxsize makes put() wait when the queue is full.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ queue.put(item), item = await queue.get(), and queue.task_done() form the common producer-consumer protocol.

reveal.text: await queue.put(item), item = await queue.get(), and queue.task_done() form the common producer-consumer protocol.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ is not thread-safe; use queue.Queue when coordinating OS threads.

reveal.text: asyncio.Queue is not thread-safe; use queue.Queue when coordinating OS threads.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ serializes access to a shared async resource so only one task holds the critical section at a time.

reveal.text: asyncio.Lock serializes access to a shared async resource so only one task holds the critical section at a time.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ with lock: state[key] += 1 automatically releases the lock even if the body raises.

reveal.text: async with lock: state[key] += 1 automatically releases the lock even if the body raises.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ lock protects a critical section; it does not make blocking synchronous work safe to run on the event loop.

reveal.text: A lock protects a critical section; it does not make blocking synchronous work safe to run on the event loop.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(func, *args) runs a synchronous callable in a worker thread and returns an awaitable for its result.

reveal.text: asyncio.to_thread(func, *args) runs a synchronous callable in a worker thread and returns an awaitable for its result.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ = await asyncio.to_thread(read_file, path) keeps blocking I/O from freezing the event loop.

reveal.text: result = await asyncio.to_thread(read_file, path) keeps blocking I/O from freezing the event loop.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ is primarily for blocking I/O under the normal GIL; CPU-bound pure Python generally needs a different parallelism strategy.

reveal.text: to_thread is primarily for blocking I/O under the normal GIL; CPU-bound pure Python generally needs a different parallelism strategy.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(delay) is an async context manager that limits the time spent awaiting operations inside its block.

reveal.text: asyncio.timeout(delay) is an async context manager that limits the time spent awaiting operations inside its block.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ with asyncio.timeout(2): result = await fetch() scopes a timeout around one or more awaits.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ try/finally around resources that must be released when a task is cancelled.

reveal.text: Use try/finally around resources that must be released when a task is cancelled.
